title: Building effective agents
about: Teaches the five workflow patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer) and when to use a real agent instead.
job: Employers want engineers who choose the simplest design that works, not a heavy framework for every problem.

lessons.t: Read: what agents are, when to use them, and when to use frameworks
Read: the augmented LLM and the workflows (chaining, routing, parallelization)
Read: orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer and agents; then Appendix 1 and 2

Task: build a prompt-chain with a gate, then an evaluator-optimizer loop for one job (for example write and critique a product description). Check: log each step and show the loop stops after at most 3 rounds

title: Foundation: Introduction to LangGraph (Python)
about: Builds stateful agents as graphs with state, memory, human-in-the-loop, sub-graphs and deployment.
job: LangGraph is a common way companies build controllable agents, and graph thinking shows you can handle state and failure.

lessons.t: Modules: Introduction (graph basics through deployment)
Modules: State and Memory (schemas, reducers, chatbot with memory)
Modules: UX and Human-in-the-Loop (streaming, breakpoints)
Modules: Building Your Assistant, Long-Term Memory, Deployment
Task: build a graph with a tool node and a human approval breakpoint before any write action. Check: run it, reject one action, and confirm nothing was written

title: AI Agents in LangGraph
about: Builds an agent from scratch, then rebuilds it in LangGraph with search tools, persistence, streaming and human approval.
job: Knowing what a framework does under the hood makes you faster at debugging agents in production.

lessons.t: Build an Agent from Scratch
LangGraph Components and Agentic Search Tools
Persistence and Streaming, Human in the Loop
Essay Writer (a multi-step agent project)
Task: port the from-scratch agent loop to a LangGraph graph with a checkpointer. Check: kill the process mid-run and resume from the saved thread

title: Multi AI Agent Systems with crewAI
about: Builds teams of role-based agents with tools, tasks and collaboration for real business jobs.

lessons.t: Agents: research-and-write crew and key elements of agents
Tools: customer support and outreach campaign crews
Tasks and collaboration: event planning and financial analysis
Project: crew that tailors job applications
Task: build a 2-agent crew (researcher and writer) for a topic you choose. Check: compare its output and token cost against one single-prompt call and write 3 lines on which won

lessons.t: Multi-agent conversation and sequential chats
Reflection and blogpost writing
Tool use, coding and financial analysis
Planning and stock report generation
Task: add a reflection step (writer plus critic) to any generator you already built. Check: score 10 outputs before and after with a simple rubric and record the change

title: Writing effective tools for AI agents
about: Teaches how to design, describe and evaluate the tools an agent calls, including naming, response size and error messages.
job: Most agent failures come from bad tool design, and engineers who can fix that are rare.

lessons.t: Read: what is a tool and how to build a prototype
Read: running and analyzing an evaluation of your tools
Read: principles (choose tools, namespacing, meaningful context, token efficiency, descriptions)
Task: write 3 tools for a small Node or Python API, then write 10 test questions. Check: run an agent on them, count wrong tool calls, then rewrite the descriptions and rerun to see the count drop

Read: core concepts and architecture
Follow: build the weather server tutorial (tools get_alerts and get_forecast)

Notebooks: tool_use (complete guide to tool use in workflows)
Notebooks: prompt_evaluations (write production prompt evals)

Building an Agent Reasoning Loop

job: Teams ask how you know your RAG app is good, and the RAG triad gives you a measurable answer.

lessons.t: Advanced RAG pipeline
RAG triad of metrics
Sentence-window retrieval
Auto-merging retrieval

title: RAG with MongoDB Vector Search
about: Explains RAG ingestion, retrieval and generation on MongoDB Vector Search, with chunking strategies and a step-by-step tutorial in Node.js.
job: A MERN developer can add RAG to an existing MongoDB app without a new database, which is a fast path to a working feature.

lessons.t: Read: why RAG and how it works with MongoDB Vector Search
Read: ingestion, retrieval and generation, and the chunking strategies table
Follow: the RAG tutorial (choose the Node.js tab)

title: Function calling and structured outputs (OpenAI API)
about: Shows how to define functions, handle model tool calls, and force output to match a JSON Schema.
job: Almost every LLM feature in a web app needs reliable JSON and tool calls, so this is daily work in the job.

lessons.t: Read: how function calling works, defining functions, best practices
Read: handling function calls and token usage
Read: Structured outputs, response_format versus function calling, versus JSON mode
Task: build an Express endpoint that extracts fields from messy text into a Zod or JSON Schema. Check: run 20 samples and count schema failures and refusals

title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications and prompt injection defenses
by: OWASP GenAI Security Project and Anthropic docs
about: Lists the ten main risks (prompt injection, excessive agency, improper output handling and more) and practical defenses.
job: Security review is a gate for shipping LLM features, and knowing this list helps you pass it.

lessons.t: Read: the OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025) list, LLM01 to LLM10
Read: Mitigate jailbreaks and prompt injections (input validation, untrusted content in tool results)
Read: Limit access to sensitive data and actions; screen tool outputs; red-team your agent

Task: plant a hidden instruction in a web page your RAG or agent reads. Check: reproduce the attack, add two defenses (untrusted content wrapping and least-privilege tools), and show the attack now fails

title: Foundation: Introduction to Agent Observability and Evaluations
about: Teaches tracing, datasets, evaluators, experiments, prompt versioning, human feedback and production monitoring for LLM apps.
job: Teams that ship agents need traces and regression tests, and few engineers can set them up.

lessons.t: Module 1: Visibility while building with tracing
Module 2: Testing and evaluation (datasets, evaluators, experiments)
Module 3 and 4: Prompt engineering and collecting human feedback
Module 5: Production observability (online evaluation, monitoring, dashboards)
Task: trace one of your own LLM routes and build a 15-example dataset. Check: change the prompt, rerun the experiment, and show which examples got better or worse

title: Define success criteria and build evaluations
about: Shows how to write measurable success criteria and grade outputs with code, human or LLM graders.
job: Evals are how teams decide to change a prompt or model without breaking things.

lessons.t: Read: define your success criteria (task fidelity, consistency, latency, price)
Read: build evaluations and the example evals
Read: grade your evaluations (code-based, human, LLM-based)
Task: write 25 test cases for one LLM feature and one code grader plus one LLM grader. Check: run on two models and report accuracy, cost and latency in a table

title: Cut LLM cost and latency: prompt caching and batching
about: Explains prompt caching (breakpoints, TTL, what invalidates cache) and the Message Batches API for 50 percent lower cost on non-urgent work.
job: LLM bills grow fast, and engineers who can cut cost and latency are valued.

lessons.t: Read: how prompt caching works, pricing, and explicit cache breakpoints
Read: caching strategies, best practices and troubleshooting
Read: Message Batches API (limits, pricing, using caching with batches)
Task: add caching to a long system prompt or tool list in one of your apps. Check: read the usage fields, show cache read tokens on the second call, and compute the cost saved over 100 calls
